headline_marked: [[12 of 16 vegetables cost Tk 80+ per kg]] in Dhaka markets, five types over Tk 100
headline: 12 of 16 vegetables cost Tk 80+ per kg in Dhaka markets, five types over Tk 100
summary: Despite some fluctuations, Dhaka's vegetable market remains unaffordable for many, with a significant number of common vegetables priced at Tk 80 or more per kilogram. Five varieties are even exceeding Tk 100.
details: Recent weeks have seen vegetable prices fluctuate, but the market is still not providing relief to consumers. A supply shortage previously pushed many vegetable prices above Tk 100 per kg, though some have since decreased with increased supply.
Currently, out of 16 types of vegetables available in the market, 12 are priced at Tk 80 or more per kilogram. Five of these varieties are selling for Tk 100 or higher.
Observations from Hatirpul and Mohammadpur's Town Hall kitchen markets in Dhaka show only four types of vegetables are available for less than Tk 80. Papaya is the cheapest, selling at Tk 40 per kg.
Among the most expensive vegetables, long eggplant costs Tk 120, round eggplant Tk 150, and tomatoes Tk 120-140 per kg. Yard-long beans, ridge gourds, and bitter gourds are all Tk 100 per kg.

Traders note that during the monsoon season, the supply of vegetables like spiny gourd, okra, pointed gourd, sponge gourd, taro, and taro stem usually increases, which should lead to lower prices. However, most of these were selling for Tk 80 per kg yesterday, with cucumbers ranging from Tk 80-100 per kg.

Prices for year-round vegetables such as papaya, bottle gourd, sweet pumpkin, and ash gourd are also relatively high. A medium bottle gourd costs Tk 70, ash gourd Tk 50-60, and sweet pumpkin Tk 60 per kg. Papaya, usually Tk 25-30, is now Tk 40.
The poultry market shows little change, with broiler chicken at Tk 190 per kg and Sonali chicken at Tk 320 in Dhaka markets. Rice prices, however, remain stable.

There's some relief in the green chili market, which was Tk 400+ two weeks ago and Tk 250-300 last week. Yesterday, it retailed at Tk 200 per kg in Hatirpul and Town Hall, and wholesaled at Tk 130-140 in Karwan Bazar, thanks to Indian imports.

Onion prices are largely unchanged, retailing at Tk 55-60 per kg depending on quality, or Tk 280-290 for five kilograms. Potato prices, however, increased by Tk 4-5 per kg from last week, selling at Tk 30 per kg in retail markets.
Egg prices remain high at Tk 150 per dozen or Tk 50 for four. A seller at Town Hall mentioned buying 100 eggs from the farm for Tk 1,220.

Sifat Sharmin, a private bank official, told Prothom Alo at Hatirpul kitchen market, "I'm buying less vegetables due to high prices. If I bought one kg before, now I buy half a kg. And I'm cooking with more gravy. Everything is expensive; there's no other way to manage."

headline_marked: [[Colombia earthquake death toll rises to 273]] after 7.4 magnitude tremor
headline: Colombia earthquake death toll rises to 273 after 7.4 magnitude tremor
summary: A powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake in western Colombia has left 273 people dead and 400 missing. Over 12,500 homes were completely destroyed, with rescue efforts continuing amidst dwindling hope.
details: The death toll from a powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake that struck western Colombia has risen to 273. Authorities have identified 227 of the deceased, but at least 400 people remain missing following the disaster.

The strong tremor hit on Monday morning local time, with its epicenter located 280 kilometers from the capital, Bogota, and approximately 96 kilometers deep. The quake was intensely felt in Bogota and several neighboring cities, followed by multiple aftershocks.

The intensity of the earthquake completely destroyed over 12,500 homes across Colombia. Additionally, approximately 75,000 residential properties sustained partial damage, exacerbating the humanitarian crisis.

Four days after the incident, the likelihood of miraculously rescuing anyone alive from the skeletal remains of the collapsed structures is diminishing daily. Despite the fading hope, rescue workers are continuing their efforts to find survivors until the very last moment.
